docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.10: Required for compatibility with the library.
  • System Requirements: Linux-based system (e.g., Ubuntu) with internet access for dependency installation.
  • Docker: Required for running the dockerised application.

docs.title: 1.1 Download and Prepare
docs.text:
• Download: Get the official Ubuntu 24.04 LTS .iso file from the Ubuntu website.
  • Create Bootable USB: Use a tool like Rufus (Windows) or balenaEtcher (Cross-platform) to create a bootable USB drive.
  • Boot: Restart your computer, enter the BIOS/UEFI settings (usually by pressing Del, F2, or F12), and select the USB drive as the boot device.

docs.title: 1.2 Installation Steps
docs.text:
1. Live Session: When the installer loads, choose the "Try Ubuntu" option first. This lets you check if everything works.

  2. Start Install: Double-click the "Install Ubuntu 24.04 LTS" icon.

  3. Third-Party Software: On the "Updates and other software" screen, check the box for "Install third-party software for graphics and Wi-Fi hardware and additional media formats." This is crucial; it helps install the initial, official NVIDIA drivers.

  4. Finish: Follow the remaining steps (disk partitioning, region, and user account) to complete the installation.

  5. Restart: When prompted, remove the USB drive and restart the computer.

docs.title: 2. System Updates and Cleanup
docs.text: This ensures you have the latest security patches and stable software versions.

docs.title: 2.1 Update the System
docs.text:
1. Open the Terminal application.

  2. Run the following commands, pressing after each one. You will be asked for your password.

    • Update the list of available software packages: 

      sudo apt update

    • Upgrade all installed packages to their latest versions: 

      sudo apt upgrade -y

    • Remove any unnecessary packages that were installed as dependencies but are no longer needed: 
      sudo apt autoremove -y

docs.title: 3. Install Docker
docs.text:
Install Docker on your system using the following Bash commands to enable dockerised application support:

sudo apt update
sudo apt install \
ca-certificates \
curl \
gnupg \
lsb-release -y

sudo mkdir -p /etc/apt/keyrings
curl -fsSL https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu/gpg | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.gpg
echo \
"deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/docker.gpg] \
https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu \
$(lsb_release -cs) stable" | \
sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/docker.list > /dev/null

sudo apt update
sudo apt install docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io docker-buildx-plugin docker-compose-plugin -y

sudo systemctl enable docker
sudo systemctl start docker

newgrp docker

docker --version
docker run hello-world

docs.title: 4. NVIDIA GPU Driver Installation
docs.text: The official Ubuntu repository contains certified, stable NVIDIA drivers. This is the safest, most reliable method.

docs.title: 4.1 Install the Recommended Driver
docs.text:
The official Ubuntu repository contains certified, stable NVIDIA drivers.

  1. Open the "Software & Updates" application (you can search for it in the main application menu).

  2. Go to the "Additional Drivers" tab.

  3. The system will scan for proprietary drivers. You should see a list of available NVIDIA drivers.

  4. Select the highest numbered, tested driver that says "(proprietary, tested)" next to it. For example, if you see nvidia-driver-550, select that one.

  5. Click "Apply Changes" and wait for the installation to finish.

  6. Reboot: You must restart the computer for the new drivers to take effect. 

    reboot

docs.title: 4.2 Verify the Installation
docs.text:
After rebooting, check that the driver is active and working.

  1. Open the Terminal.

  2. Run the NVIDIA System Management Interface tool: 

    nvidia-smi

  3. Success: If you see a table showing your GPU model (e.g., RTX 6000 Ada), the driver version, and current GPU usage, the installation was successful.

docs.title: 5.1 Install Python 3.10:
docs.text:
Install Python 3.10 using the following commands in a Bash terminal:

sudo apt update
sudo apt upgrade
sudo apt autoremove
sudo add-apt-repository ppa:deadsnakes/ppa
sudo apt update
sudo apt install python3.10 python3.10-venv python3.10-distutils python3.10-dev -y

curl -sS https://bootstrap.pypa.io/get-pip.py | sudo python3.10

docs.title: 5.2 Install Development Dependencies
docs.text:
Open the Terminal and install the tools needed for compiling software and managing Python environments: 

sudo apt install build-essential git cmake python3-dev

docs.title: 5.3 Use Virtual Environments (Recommended)
docs.text:
Virtual Environments (venv) create a separate, isolated folder for each Python project. This prevents conflicts between projects and keeps the system Python clean.

  1. Create a Project Folder: 
    mkdir ~/my_python_project 
cd ~/my_python_project
  2. Create the Virtual Environment: Use the system's python3 to create a virtual environment named .venv. 
    python3.10 -m venv .venv
  3. Activate the Environment: You must activate the environment every time you start 
    source .doc_env/bin/activate

docs.title: 6. Application installation
docs.text: For the application installation first the application has to be downloaded and then the required packages have to be installed in the virtual environment

docs.title: 6.1 Copy the Repository Zip:
docs.text:
Navigate to your target directory, copy the code zip, extract the code and open the IDP directory: 

cd IDP

docs.title: 6.2 Install Dependencies:
docs.text:
Run the following commands in the same terminal to install the necessary packages: 

pip install -r reqirements.txt

docs.title: 6.3 Run Frontend:
docs.text:
To run the frontend open the idp-frontend directory and run the frontend file in bash:
```bash
cd IDP/jsw-frontend/idp-frontend
npm run dev
```

docs.title: 6.4 Run Python Connection file:
docs.text:
To start the connection between frontend and backend run the connection.py file:
```bash
python3 IDP/infrastructure/message_queue/connection.py
```
